content: Crash-safe local file writes use the write-to-temp-then-rename pattern: write full content to a temp file in the same directory, flush/close it, then rename() over the destination -- POSIX rename is atomic so a crash mid-write leaves either the old file intact or the fully-written new one, never a partial file. Cleanup logic should scan for and delete orphaned temp files left behind by an interrupted write (e.g. on next app launch). Flutter has no built-in atomic-write helper; must be implemented manually via dart:io File + path_provider.
